name: glslViewer
notes: 2026-11-01: Renders fragment shaders or shaded models to PNG sequences with explicit time stepping.
2026-11-01: GPU float differences can break bit-identical fixtures; use perceptual tolerances.
2026-11-01: Triage: assess. Report rates it worth cataloguing.

evidence.result: 8 frames 128x96 (2x Retina backing); 16 pixel probes within 2/channel of analytic; 8 distinct frames; rerun and 0.5 s sub-range hashes identical; renderer Apple M3 Pro
evidence.scope: Headless sequence export of a hand-written u_time shader: 8 PNGs at 128x96 (2x Retina), pixel probes, reruns and 0.5 s sub-range match; no screenshot, time cmd or window; macOS arm64 only

summary: Interactive and command-line GLSL shader viewer that can render shader output to image sequences with time input. It offers a small native route for capturing shader sketches; GPU and driver differences affect reproducibility.
use_when: Render GLSL shader sketches from the command line
Capture time-stepped shader output as image sequences
avoid_when: Use Three.js for richer browser-based shader scenes
Use glslang for shader compilation and validation only

assessment.rationale: Official GitHub releases list 3.5.2 dated 2026-02-07. The README documents headless rendering and image/PNG-sequence export; documentation assessment only.
